assembly_instructions: 1) Start from the FPGA PCB substrate (14x9 m floorplan) and overlay the silicon-die outline plate that bounds the placed-and-routed logic; on the -X edge seat the host interface: a PCIe x16 gold-finger edge connector feeding a host DMA/PCIe controller block, the boundary where coefficient vectors enter and transformed results leave. 2) Drive the controller into the forward-NTT input FIFO and natural-order output FIFO, then mount the eight interleaved BRAM banks along the left edge at 1.1 m pitch between them. 3) Drop the conflict-free crossbar network as a vertical spine just inboard of the banks, and place the inverse-NTT N^-1 scaling unit on its output side. 4) Build the open butterfly-array frame: lay a thin floor across the array, then bolt the two longitudinal steel rails and the mid cross-brace so the chassis stays open from above; populate the eight parallel butterfly lanes (one per BRAM bank) by wiring each DSP modular multiplier into its symmetric modular adder (dark anodized) and subtractor (brushed steel), then both into the pipeline register. 5) Place the shared modular-reduction stage to the right as two distinct members: first the cylindrical Barrett q-multiplier spanning all eight lanes, then the boxy shift/subtract+correction member, wired from every pipeline register. 6) Route the operand-return bus from the reduction member back over the array to the crossbar (grounded by a standoff post onto the reduction member), and route the operand-read bus from the crossbar east into the multiplier column (grounded by its own standoff onto the array frame); cap each with a direction arrow so the read/twiddle/return dataflow triad is fully visible and the conflict-free read-modify-write loop is closed. 7) On the right, install the twiddle-factor ROM and route a brass broadcast feeder west to the rail spanning the multiplier column (grounded by a standoff onto the array frame) so one fetched factor fans out to all eight multipliers; then add the address-generation unit, the radix-2/4 config selector, the schedule/FSM controller and the clock PLL. 8) For inspection, lift one butterfly cluster onto two riser posts into an exploded view above the array (multiply->add/sub->register), offset toward the +Z half so it clears the central lanes in plan view, and clamp the ten-fin exploded aluminum heatsink onto its riser stub above the die.

params.modulus_q_note: Source gives only '14-bit NTT-friendly prime'; reproduction fixes q=12289=3*2^12+1, the canonical 14-bit prime with 2048 | (q-1) so 2N-th roots of unity exist for a 1024-point transform.
params.transform_flavor: Unstated in source; PQC/HE context implies negacyclic (psi = 2N=2048-th primitive root, omega = psi^2 the N-th root). Cyclic is the degenerate fallback the earlier functional impls used and is a likely mismatch.
params.twiddle_root_constraints: psi^2048 ≡ 1 and psi^1024 ≡ -1 (mod q); omega = psi^2; any generator satisfying these is a valid reproduction choice.

pipeline_latency_cycles.note: Reproduction defaults pending the paper's reported cycle counts.

ops: Barrett modular reduction: q-multiply then shift/subtract+correct
properties: conflict-free memory mapping: arbitrary radix and arbitrary #BU access the interleaved BRAM banks with no bank conflict
twiddle-factor reuse via a rearranged loop structure
radix-4 uses 33% fewer modular multiplications and 20% fewer modular add/sub than radix-2
~50% of butterfly hardware saved via symmetric operators
NTT followed by INTT (with N^-1 scaling) is the identity
spec.notes: Authoritative claims from CFNTT, TCHES 2022 issue 1, pp.94-126 (Chen et al., Tsinghua). The exact modulus q is given in the source only as a 14-bit NTT-friendly prime; the 1024-pt benchmark uses a 14-bit q. Verification auto-selects the SMT backend because this is a digital/compute design (NTT datapath), not a mechanical machine.

info.japanese_name: CFNTT スケーラブル基数2/4 NTT 乗算アーキテクチャ (FPGA)
info.english_name: CFNTT: Scalable Radix-2/4 NTT Multiplication Architecture
info.summary: An FPGA accelerator for the Number Theoretic Transform that combines a conflict-free memory mapping scheme with parallel radix-4 butterfly units, the polynomial-multiplication engine behind lattice post-quantum cryptography and homomorphic encryption.
info.description: CFNTT is an algorithm-hardware co-designed NTT core proposed by Chen et al. (Tsinghua University) in TCHES 2022. Its central contribution is a conflict-free memory mapping scheme that lets an arbitrary radix and an arbitrary number of parallel butterfly units access an interleaved BRAM system without bank conflicts, removing the bit-reversal cost and reducing memory footprint by reusing twiddle factors across a rearranged loop structure.
info.description2: Built on this scheme, the architecture realizes a scalable radix-2 / radix-4 datapath. A dedicated schedule cuts radix-4 modular additions/subtractions by 20% and modular multiplications by 33%, while exploiting symmetric operators saves nearly 50% of the butterfly hardware. For a 1024-point, 14-bit NTT with 8 parallel butterfly units, the radix-4 core achieves roughly 2.2x/1.2x/1.1x/1.9x lower LUT/FF/DSP/BRAM area-time product than the radix-2 core.

facts.label: Board footprint
facts.value: 14 x 9 units; BRAM banks and butterfly lanes at 1.1 pitch

sources.title: CFNTT: Scalable Radix-2/4 NTT Multiplication Architecture (TCHES 2022)

parts.name: FPGA PCB Substrate
parts.role: The 14x9 m FPGA board floorplan carrying every NTT datapath block and the routing between them.

parts.name: FPGA Silicon Die Outline
parts.role: Silicon-die outline of the FPGA; every block standing above this plate is placed-and-routed logic inside the die boundary, marking the chip extent on the board.

parts.name: PCIe x16 Host Edge Connector
parts.role: PCIe x16 gold-finger edge connector protruding from the board's -X edge; the physical host interface where the host streams raw coefficient vectors into the accelerator and reads transformed results back, marking this die as an NTT coprocessor card rather than a standalone chip.

parts.name: Host DMA / PCIe Controller
parts.role: Host-side DMA / PCIe controller block on the board edge that buffers the edge-connector traffic and drives the forward-NTT input FIFO and drains the natural-order output FIFO, the data origin and sink of the whole datapath.

parts.name: BRAM Bank 0
parts.role: Interleaved ~18 Kb block RAM holding polynomial coefficients under conflict-free addressing; feeds butterfly lane 0 and the input stream head.

params.addressing: offset o(i)=i>>3 within bank b(i)=(i+(i>>3)) mod 8

parts.name: BRAM Bank 1
parts.role: Interleaved BRAM bank in the eight-way conflict-free memory system feeding butterfly lane 1.

parts.name: BRAM Bank 2
parts.role: Interleaved BRAM bank addressed by the mapping scheme so no two parallel butterflies collide; feeds lane 2.

parts.name: BRAM Bank 3
parts.role: Interleaved BRAM bank in the eight-way conflict-free memory system feeding butterfly lane 3.

parts.name: BRAM Bank 4
parts.role: Interleaved BRAM bank in the eight-way conflict-free memory system feeding butterfly lane 4.

parts.name: BRAM Bank 5

parts.name: BRAM Bank 6
parts.role: Interleaved BRAM bank feeding lane 6 and the natural-order write-back path.

parts.name: BRAM Bank 7
parts.role: Interleaved BRAM bank providing the natural-order write-back path to the output FIFO (no bit-reversal); feeds lane 7.

parts.name: Forward-NTT Input FIFO
parts.role: Streams raw input coefficients from the host controller into the head BRAM banks in natural order at the start of the forward NTT pass.

parts.name: Natural-Order Output FIFO
parts.role: Drains transformed coefficients out of the tail banks in natural order back to the host controller, eliminating the bit-reversal pass.

parts.name: Conflict-Free Crossbar Network
parts.role: Permutation crossbar (8x8) implementing the conflict-free mapping, routing operands between the eight banks and eight butterfly lanes and accepting reduced results back over the return bus.

spec.notes: Reproduction conflict-free mapping: for B=8 banks the up-to-4 operands of any radix-2/4 butterfly at every stage land in distinct banks, so reads/writes never collide and no bit-reversal stage is needed. The paper's exact bank-index/offset functions (its headline Sec. III result) are not transcribed in the source; this XOR/rotate-style map satisfies the asserted no-conflict property and is rebuildable by a CS student.

parts.name: Inverse-NTT N^-1 Scaling Unit
parts.role: Inverse-NTT (INTT) stage: multiplies the returning coefficients by the modular inverse of the transform length (N^-1 mod q) so the same butterfly array performs both forward and inverse transforms.

parts.name: Butterfly-Array Open Frame Floor
parts.role: Thin open floor of the butterfly-array frame; together with the two longitudinal rails and the cross-brace it forms an open chassis spanning all eight parallel lanes, exposing every DSP multiplier and symmetric add/sub operator from above (X-ray cutaway).

params.lane_pipeline: mult(3) -> add/sub(1) -> reg(1); shared Barrett reduction adds 4 -> lane_total 9 cycles
params.datapath_dir: +X: operands read at -X multiplier column, results latched at +X register column

parts.name: Butterfly-Array Left Rail
parts.role: Left longitudinal frame rail running the full depth of the array just outboard of the DSP multiplier column; a real chassis member that frames the open lanes without enclosing them, so every multiplier stays visible from above.

parts.name: Butterfly-Array Right Rail
parts.role: Right longitudinal frame rail running the full depth of the array just outboard of the pipeline-register column; paired with the left rail it carries the lane loads to the board while leaving the datapath exposed.

parts.name: Butterfly-Array Cross-Brace
parts.role: Mid-span cross-brace tying the two array rails together across the lane-3/lane-4 gap, stiffening the open frame; placed in the empty central gap so it crosses no lane and hides no operator.

parts.name: Twiddle Broadcast Rail Standoff
parts.role: Short standoff post in the central lane-3/4 gap grounding the elevated brass twiddle broadcast rail down onto the open array frame, so the twiddle fan-out reads as physically supported wiring rather than a floating line in the elevation views.

parts.name: Operand-Read Bus Standoff
parts.role: Short standoff post tying the elevated operand-read bus down onto the array frame between its crossbar seat and the multiplier-column arrow, so the read channel is physically supported and the read/twiddle/return routing triad all reads as real wiring.

parts.name: DSP Modular Multiplier 0
parts.role: DSP-slice modular multiplier applying twiddle factors at the front of butterfly lane 0, feeding its symmetric adder/subtractor pair; 14x14-bit product, 3-cycle latency.

params.function: t = a * w mod-pending (Barrett reduction shared downstream)

parts.name: Twiddle Broadcast Rail
parts.role: Elevated broadcast rail running the full depth of the multiplier column, fanning the single fetched twiddle factor down to all eight DSP modular multipliers each cycle so each root of unity is read once and reused; supported on a central standoff post onto the array frame.

parts.name: Twiddle Broadcast Feeder
parts.role: Routes each twiddle factor fetched once from the ROM westward to the broadcast rail above the multiplier column, the physical embodiment of the factor-reuse the rearranged loop schedule exploits.

parts.name: Operand-Read Routing Bus
parts.role: Operand-read bus carrying source coefficients fetched conflict-free from the crossbar eastward into the DSP multiplier-column inputs; together with the brass twiddle rail and the blue return bus it makes the full read/twiddle/return dataflow triad visible and is the read half of the read-modify-write loop, supported on a standoff post onto the array frame.

parts.name: Operand-Read Direction Arrow
parts.role: Arrowhead at the multiplier-column end of the read bus, pointing +X into the DSP multipliers to mark that operands flow from the crossbar into the butterfly inputs (not the reverse), making the read path directional.

parts.name: Exploded Butterfly Cluster Baseplate
parts.role: EXPLODED VIEW floating above the array on two riser posts, offset toward the +Z half of the array so it clears the central lanes (3-4) in plan view: one of the eight identical butterfly lanes lifted off the board to expose its left-to-right datapath (DSP multiply -> symmetric add/sub -> pipeline register).

parts.name: Exploded-View Riser Post A
parts.role: Thin support post linking the array baseplate to the lifted exploded baseplate, making the exploded relationship explicit in the elevation views.

parts.name: Exploded-View Riser Post B
parts.role: Second support post for the exploded butterfly lane, anchoring the lifted baseplate over the array so it does not read as floating.

parts.name: Exploded DSP Modular Multiplier
parts.role: Exploded view, first datapath stage: the DSP-slice modular multiplier applies the twiddle factor to one operand, then feeds the symmetric adder and subtractor.

parts.name: Exploded Symmetric Modular Adder
parts.role: Exploded view, second stage: symmetric modular adder (dark anodized = the sum path) producing the sum output of the radix-4 butterfly, latched into the pipeline register.

parts.name: Exploded Symmetric Modular Subtractor
parts.role: Exploded view, second stage: symmetric modular subtractor (brushed steel = the difference path) reusing the adder's operands (the ~50% hardware-saving trick), latched into the pipeline register.

parts.name: Exploded Pipeline Register
parts.role: Exploded view, final stage: pipeline register that latches the butterfly result and feeds the shared modular-reduction spine; this lane is one of eight identical instances on the array below.

parts.name: Modular Reduction — Barrett q-Multiplier
parts.role: First member of the shared modular-reduction stage: a cylindrical Barrett quotient-multiplier spine running the full depth of the array, estimating t = floor(x*mu / 2^28) (mu=21843) for every incoming butterfly product before correction.

spec.notes: Reduces 28-bit products of two sub-q operands; computes the quotient estimate t here, with subtract+correct done in mod_red_subshift. mu/k are reproduction values for q=12289.

parts.name: Modular Reduction — Shift/Subtract & Correct
parts.role: Second member of the reduction stage: computes r = x - t*q and applies up to two conditional subtractions of q to bring results into [0, q) before returning them to the crossbar.

ops: while r >= q: r -= q   (<=2 iterations)
spec.notes: Completes the Barrett reduction begun in mod_red_mult.

parts.name: Operand-Return Bus Standoff
parts.role: Short standoff post grounding the elevated operand-return bus down onto the shift/subtract reduction member, so the overhead return routing is physically supported rather than floating in the elevation views.

parts.name: Operand-Return Routing Bus
parts.role: Elevated return-routing channel carrying reduced coefficients from the shift/subtract member back across the array to the crossbar, closing the conflict-free read-modify-write loop (reduction -> crossbar -> banks).

parts.name: Operand-Return Direction Arrow
parts.role: Arrowhead at the crossbar end of the return bus, pointing -X into the crossbar to mark that reduced operands flow from the reduction stage back to the crossbar (not the other way), making the read-modify-write loop directional.

parts.name: Twiddle-Factor ROM
parts.role: On-chip ROM storing precomputed roots of unity (psi^k / omega^k), reused across the rearranged loop so each factor is fetched once and broadcast over the feeder/rail to all eight multipliers.

params.stored: omega^k stage twiddles for k=0..N-1; psi^k 2N-th-root pre/post-twist factors for the negacyclic case
params.addressing: address = f(stage s, butterfly-block index); one fetch reused across all 8 lanes per block

spec.notes: Depth N=1024 covers every stage twiddle without bit-reversal. Reproduction stores psi powers; the source states reuse via the rearranged loop but does not give the table contents or primitive root.

parts.name: Address Generation Unit
parts.role: Generates the conflict-free read/write addresses and bank indices (b(i)=(i+(i>>3)) mod 8, offset i>>3) that realize the memory-mapping scheme each cycle.

params.twiddle_addr: derived from stage s and block index, shared by all active lanes

spec.notes: Drives the crossbar permutation and the twiddle-ROM address; stride switches with the radix selector (radix-4 doubles the per-pass stage span).

parts.name: Radix-2/4 Config Selector
parts.role: Configuration register selecting radix (2 or 4) and the number of active parallel butterfly units (up to 8).

params.lane_map_radix4: two adjacent radix-2 lanes fuse into one 4-input/3-twiddle radix-4 butterfly -> 8 lanes = 4 radix-4 BUs per cycle

spec.notes: Radix-4 fuses two consecutive NTT stages into one pass, the source of the 33% fewer multiplications and 20% fewer add/sub vs radix-2; selector also sets address strides in addr_gen and twiddle indexing.

parts.name: Conflict-Free Schedule/FSM Controller
parts.role: Finite-state controller driving the rearranged loop order that cuts radix-4 mults by 33% and add/sub by 20% while keeping memory accesses conflict-free.

ops: for s in stages: for block in groups_sharing_one_twiddle: { fetch w once; parallel for bu in 0..7: butterfly(bu) }
spec.notes: The factor-constant inner block is what lets one twiddle fetch be reused across all 8 lanes. Exact state-transition table and loop bounds are reconstructed; the source asserts the 33%/20% savings only as a property.

parts.name: Clock PLL
parts.role: Phase-locked loop generating the core datapath clock for the pipelined eight-lane butterfly array.
